newsitem.title: USA: Carroll O'Connor found not guilty in slander suit.
newsitem.headline: Carroll O'Connor found not guilty in slander suit.

text.p: A county court jury found actor Carroll O'Connor not guilty of slander Friday in a case brought by a man O'Connor accused of contributing to his son's suicide by supplying him with cocaine.

The man, Harry Perzigian, brought the suit against O'Connor charging that the actor engaged in a malicious bid to avenge the suicide of O'Connor's 32-year-old son, Hugh. In television interviews, O'Connor had called Perzigian "a partner in murder."

The jury also cleared the 72-year-old O'Connor of charges of intentionally inflicting emotional distress on Perzigian, a songwriter who served a jail term for drug use and who has admitted occasionally giving cocaine to Hugh O'Connor.
Lawyers for O'Connor, who is best-known for playing television's crusty Archie Bunker, called Perzigian Hugh O'Connor's "cocaine connection."

In TV interviews, the actor called Perzigian "a partner in murder" and "a lawbreaker." He also gave out his address and showed his photo. O'Connor said in one interview: "Harry Perzigian, you sleaze-ball. We're going to get you" and "I want to hurt him in the worst way."

In her closing argument, O'Connor's attorney, Lucy Inman, told the jury to consider the comments as from a grieving father who had lost his only son and to view the case as a blow in the battle against drugs.
